intro.title: House Robber
intro.body: In this lesson, you'll implement the 'House Robber' algorithm, which determines the maximum amount of money a robber can steal from a row of houses without robbing two adjacent houses. You'll learn to use dynamic programming, a technique for solving problems by breaking them into smaller subproblems and storing their results. The main constructs involved are arrays for storing house values and a loop to iteratively build the solution. This exercise will help you practice problem decomposition and efficient state management in JavaScript.
intro.usecase: The House Robber algorithm pattern appears in resource allocation systems where you need to maximize value while respecting constraints. For example, in financial portfolio optimization dashboards, you might need to select investments while avoiding adjacent risky assets. In scheduling tools, you could optimize meeting times without overlapping adjacent slots. This dynamic programming approach helps developers build efficient recommendation engines, resource planners, and optimization interfaces that make intelligent selections under constraints.
